# owo_colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/

## Expand description

This crate provides [ OwoColorize](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html), an extension trait for colorizing a
given type.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
// Foreground colors
println!("My number is {:#x}!", 10.green());
// Background colors
println!("My number is not {}!", 4.on_red());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#generically-color)Generically color

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
use owo_colors::colors::*;
// Generically color
println!("My number might be {}!", 4.fg::<Black>().bg::<Yellow>());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#stylize)Stylize

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
println!("{}", "strikethrough".strikethrough());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#only-style-on-supported-terminals)Only Style on Supported Terminals

```
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, Stream::Stdout};
println!(
    "{}",
    "colored blue if a supported terminal"
        .if_supports_color(Stdout, |text| text.bright_blue())
);
```
Supports `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` environment variables, checks if it’s a tty, checks
if it’s running in CI (and thus likely supports color), and checks which terminal is being
used. (Note: requires `supports-colors` feature)

[§](https://docs.rs#style-objects)Style Objects

owo-colors also features the ability to create a [ Style](https://docs.rs/struct.Style.html) object and use it to
apply the same set of colors/effects to any number of things to display.

```
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, Style};
let my_style = Style::new()
    .red()
    .on_white()
    .strikethrough();
let text = "red text, white background, struck through";
println!("{}", text.style(my_style));
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [colored](https://docs.rs/colored/index.html)
- Module for drop-in `colored``colored`
- [colors](https://docs.rs/colors/index.html)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [BgColor](https://docs.rs/struct.BgColorDisplay.html)- Display
- Transparent wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does,
with the addition of changing the background color. Recommended to be constructed using
`OwoColorize`
- [BgDyn](https://docs.rs/struct.BgDynColorDisplay.html)- Color - Display
- Wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does, with the addition of changing the background color. Is not recommended unless compile-time coloring is not an option.
- [Combo](https://docs.rs/struct.ComboColorDisplay.html)- Color - Display
- A wrapper type which applies both a foreground and background color
- [Combo](https://docs.rs/struct.ComboDynColorDisplay.html)- DynColor - Display
- Wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does, with the addition of changing the foreground and background color.
- [FgColor](https://docs.rs/struct.FgColorDisplay.html)- Display
- Transparent wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does,
with the addition of changing the foreground color. Recommended to be constructed using
`OwoColorize`
- [FgDyn](https://docs.rs/struct.FgDynColorDisplay.html)- Color - Display
- Wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does, with the addition of changing the foreground color. Is not recommended unless compile-time coloring is not an option.
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseColorError.html)- Color - Error
- An error for when the color can not be parsed from a string at runtime
- [Rgb](https://docs.rs/struct.Rgb.html)
- Available RGB colors for use with `OwoColorize::color``OwoColorize::on_color`
- [Style](https://docs.rs/struct.Style.html)
- A pre-computed style that can be applied to a struct using `OwoColorize::style`
- [Style](https://docs.rs/struct.StylePrefixFormatter.html)- Prefix - Formatter
- Formatter for the prefix of a `Style`
- [Style](https://docs.rs/struct.StyleSuffixFormatter.html)- Suffix - Formatter
- Formatter for the suffix of a `Style`

- A wrapper type which applies a `Style`
- [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.StyledList.html)- List
- A collection of `Styled`
- [Supports](https://docs.rs/struct.SupportsColorsDisplay.html)- Colors - Display - `supports-colors`
- A display wrapper which applies a transformation based on if the given stream supports colored terminal output

# owo-colors 4.3.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/owo-colors/latest

# Colors

A zero-allocation no_std-compatible zero-cost way to add color to your Rust terminal to make people go owo.

**Supports:**

- All std/core formatters
-  Optional checking for if a terminal supports colors
- Enabled for CI
- Disabled by default for non-terminal outputs
-  Overridable by `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR`environment variables
-  Overridable programmatically via `set_override`

- Dependency-less by default
- 100% safe code
-  Most functions are `const`
- Hand picked names for all ANSI (4-bit) and Xterm (8-bit) colors
- Support for RGB colors
- Set colors at compile time by generics or at runtime by value
-  All ANSI colors
- Basic support (normal and bright variants)
- Xterm support (high compatibility and 256 colors)
- Truecolor support (modern, 48-bit color)

- Styling (underline, strikethrough, etc)

owo-colors is also more-or-less a drop-in replacement for
[colored](https://crates.io/crates/colored), allowing colored to work in a
no_std environment. No allocations or dependencies required because embedded
systems deserve to be pretty too uwu.

To add to your Cargo.toml:

```
 = "4"
```
## Example

```
use OwoColorize;
```
## Generic colors

```
use OwoColorize;
use *;
```
## Stylize

```
use OwoColorize;
println!;
```
## Only Style on Supported Terminals

```
use ;
println!;
```
Supports `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` environment variables, checks if it's a tty,
checks if it's running in CI (and thus likely supports color), and checks which
terminal is being used. (Note: requires `supports-colors` feature)

## Minimum supported Rust version (MSRV)

The MSRV of owo-colors is **Rust 1.81**.

This library has a conservative MSRV policy — Rust versions from the last 12 months will be supported (features available in newer versions will be gated by `build.rs`), the MSRV will only be bumped if required, and if the MSRV is bumped it will always occur with a new minor version.

# supports_color - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/supports-color/^3.0.0/

## Expand description

Detects whether a terminal supports color, and gives details about that
support. It takes into account the `NO_COLOR` environment variable.

This crate is a Rust port of [@sindresorhus](https://github.com/sindresorhus)’
[NPM package by the same name](https://npm.im/supports-color).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use supports_color::Stream;
if let Some(support) = supports_color::on(Stream::Stdout) {
    if support.has_16m {
        println!("16 million (RGB) colors are supported");
    } else if support.has_256 {
        println!("256-bit colors are supported.");
    } else if support.has_basic {
        println!("Only basic ANSI colors are supported.");
    }
} else {
    println!("No color support.");
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Color](https://docs.rs/struct.ColorLevel.html)- Level
- Color level support details.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Stream](https://docs.rs/enum.Stream.html)
- possible stream sources

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [on](https://docs.rs/fn.on.html)
- Returns a [ColorLevel](https://docs.rs/struct.ColorLevel.html)if a[Stream](https://docs.rs/enum.Stream.html)supports terminal colors.
- [on_](https://docs.rs/fn.on_cached.html)- cached
- Returns a [ColorLevel](https://docs.rs/struct.ColorLevel.html)if a[Stream](https://docs.rs/enum.Stream.html)supports terminal colors, caching the result to be returned from then on.

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (4c9d2bfe4 2026-07-01)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# colored - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/colored

## Expand description

Coloring terminal so simple, you already know how to do it !

```
use colored::Colorize;
"this is blue".blue();
"this is red".red();
"this is red on blue".red().on_blue();
"this is also red on blue".on_blue().red();
"you can use truecolor values too!".truecolor(0, 255, 136);
"background truecolor also works :)".on_truecolor(135, 28, 167);
"you can also make bold text".bold();
println!("{} {} {}", "or use".cyan(), "any".italic().yellow(), "string type".cyan());
"or change advice. This is red".yellow().blue().red();
"or clear things up. This is default color and style".red().bold().clear();
"purple and magenta are the same".purple().magenta();
"bright colors are also allowed".bright_blue().on_bright_white();
"you can specify color by string".color("blue").on_color("red");
"and so are normal and clear".normal().clear();
String::from("this also works!").green().bold();
format!("{:30}", "format works as expected. This will be padded".blue());
format!("{:.3}", "and this will be green but truncated to 3 chars".green());
```
See [the  Colorize trait](https://docs.rs/trait.Colorize.html) for all the methods.

Note: The methods of [ Colorize](https://docs.rs/trait.Colorize.html), when used on

[’s, return](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)

`str`[’s. See](https://docs.rs/struct.ColoredString.html)

`ColoredString`[to learn more about them and what you can do with them beyond continuing to use](https://docs.rs/struct.ColoredString.html)

`ColoredString`[to further modify them.](https://docs.rs/trait.Colorize.html)

`Colorize`## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use self::customcolors::`- [CustomColor](https://docs.rs/customcolors/struct.CustomColor.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [control](https://docs.rs/control/index.html)
- A couple of functions to enable and disable coloring.
- [customcolors](https://docs.rs/customcolors/index.html)
- Custom colors support.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Colored](https://docs.rs/struct.ColoredString.html)- String
- A string that may have color and/or style applied to it.
- [Style](https://docs.rs/struct.Style.html)
- A combinatorial style such as bold, italics, dimmed, etc.

- The 8 standard colors.

# harn_lsp - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/harn-lsp/0.8.168/harn_lsp/

## Expand description

Harn language server.

Exposed as a library so the single multi-call `harn` binary can dispatch
into the LSP server when launched under the `harn-lsp` name (see
`harn-cli`’s `main`), instead of shipping a second fully-linked binary.
The thin `src/main.rs` shim keeps `harn-lsp` buildable as its own binary
for local development (`cargo run -p harn-lsp`).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [run](https://docs.rs/fn.run.html)
- Run the Harn language server over stdio until the client disconnects.

# yoagent_state - Rust

## Expand description

Simple but effective state and lineage for long-running agents.

`yoagent-state` stores append-only events and derives a small semantic graph
for patches, evals, decisions, artifacts, and project references. Git and the
filesystem remain the source of truth for concrete project changes.

[§](https://docs.rs#scirs-biological-alignment-advanced)SciRS Biological Alignment (Advanced)

High-rigor alignment of biological structures and sequences. No simplified algorithms.

This crate provides:

# ordeal - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ordeal/0.3.0/ordeal/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#ordeal)Ordeal

`ordeal` (meaning “verdict / judgment”) is a specialized,
**certificate-checked** QF_BV SMT solver for the [PulseEngine](https://github.com/pulseengine) toolchain. It
exists to replace the Z3 static-link build pain that loom (verified WASM
optimizer) and synth (verified WASM→ARM codegen) carry today — grounding:
loom issue #246.

[§](https://docs.rs#design-in-one-paragraph)Design in one paragraph

An **untrusted solver** emits a machine-checkable **LRAT UNSAT
certificate**; a small **formally-verified checker** validates it. Only the
checker is trusted (the CompCert certifying-algorithm pattern; blueprint =
Lean 4 `bv_decide`, OOPSLA 2025). Z3 is demoted to a differential *oracle*
and benchmark *rival*, not the production engine. The pipeline is: term
graph → bit-blast → AIG → CNF (Tseitin) → SAT → LRAT → verified checker.

[§](https://docs.rs#modules)Modules

- `term`
- `solver`- `check-sat`interface and result types.
- `eval`
- `aig`
- `blast`
- `cnf`
- `sat`
- `lrat`- `ordeal-lrat`crate (the sole trusted component) validates it before any- `Unsat`is returned.
- [`oracle`] — the Z3 differential oracle (behind the`oracle`feature).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use solver::`- [Certificate](https://docs.rs/solver/struct.Certificate.html);
- `pub use solver::`- [CheckResult](https://docs.rs/solver/enum.CheckResult.html);
- `pub use solver::`- [Model](https://docs.rs/solver/struct.Model.html);
- `pub use solver::`- [Solver](https://docs.rs/solver/struct.Solver.html);
- `pub use term::`- [BoolTerm](https://docs.rs/term/enum.BoolTerm.html);
- `pub use term::`- [BvTerm](https://docs.rs/term/enum.BvTerm.html);
- `pub use term::`- [Sort](https://docs.rs/term/struct.Sort.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules-1)

- [aig](https://docs.rs/aig/index.html)
- And-Inverter Graph with structural hashing and constant folding (DES-002).
- [blast](https://docs.rs/blast/index.html)
- Bit-blasting rules: each QF_BV operation lowered to AIG gates (DES-005..DES-009), one module per op family.
- [cnf](https://docs.rs/cnf/index.html)
- CNF representation and the Tseitin encoder (DES-003).
- [eval](https://docs.rs/eval/index.html)
- Concrete evaluator for the closed QF_BV fragment — the executable SMT-LIB semantics (DES-001).
- [lrat](https://docs.rs/lrat/index.html)
- LRAT certificate emission from the CDCL proof trace (DES-013).
- [sat](https://docs.rs/sat/index.html)
- The pure-Rust CDCL SAT core (DES-004) — primary engine on every target.
- [sliver](https://docs.rs/sliver/index.html)
- The loom array/UF sliver (P3) — an extended query layer that is
**preprocessed away**into the closed QF_BV core before bit-blasting.
- [solver](https://docs.rs/solver/index.html)
- The one-shot solver interface and the P1 pipeline dispatcher (DES-012).
- [term](https://docs.rs/term/index.html)
- The `ordeal`term language: the closed QF_BV fragment from loom issue #246.

# ordeal_lrat - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ordeal-lrat/0.3.0/ordeal_lrat/

## Expand description

Ordeal’s LRAT certificate checker — **the sole trusted component**.

The ordeal solver is untrusted: an `Unsat` answer is believed only when
this checker has validated an LRAT certificate for it. This crate is
written to be translated to Lean 4 (via Aeneas) and formally verified, so
everything here is deliberately small, simple, and obviously correct:
no `unsafe`, no dependencies, no cleverness.

[§](https://docs.rs#supported-dialect-textual-lrat-rup-only)Supported dialect: textual LRAT, **RUP-only**

**LOUD LIMITATION:** this checker supports only RUP (Reverse Unit
Propagation) addition steps. RAT steps — recognised by *negative* clause
ids in the hint list — are **rejected** with
[ CheckError::RatUnsupported](https://docs.rs/enum.CheckError.html#variant.RatUnsupported). This is deliberate: ordeal’s CDCL engine
emits RUP-only proofs, and rejecting is always sound (we may refuse a
valid certificate, we never accept an invalid one).

Accepted line forms (whitespace-separated integers, one step per line;
blank lines and lines starting with `c` are skipped as comments):

- Addition: `<id> <lit>* 0 <hint>* 0`— adds the clause`<lit>*`with id`<id>`, justified by unit propagation through the clauses named by`<hint>*`, in order.
- Deletion: `<id> d <id>* 0`— marks the named clauses dead. The leading`<id>`is informational (as emitted by drat-trim) and is not checked.

Clause ids are 1-based: original clause `i` of the input CNF (0-based)
has id `i + 1`; each addition step must then use exactly the next
sequential id (this is what ordeal emits; sparse ids are rejected).

[§](https://docs.rs#what-checked-means)What “checked” means

An addition step `C` with hints `h1..hk` is verified by assuming the
negation of every literal of `C` and then unit-propagating through the
hint clauses in order: each hint must be either *falsified* (conflict —
the step is verified, so CNF ∧ ¬C is unsat, i.e. CNF ⊨ C) or *unit*
(its single unassigned literal is assigned true). Anything else —
a satisfied hint, a hint with two or more unassigned literals, running
out of hints, a dead or unknown id — rejects the certificate.

The whole certificate is accepted iff it parses in full AND some verified
addition step adds the **empty clause** (checking stops at that step;
parsed trailing steps are ignored). Parsing everything first is stricter
than strictly necessary and always sound (extra rejections only).

[§](https://docs.rs#structure-parser-vs-kernel)Structure: parser vs kernel

The crate is split for the formal proof (issue #12): the [ kernel](https://docs.rs/kernel/index.html)
module is the string-free checking core — the Aeneas → Lean translation
target carrying the soundness theorem — and this file is the untrusted
text parser feeding it. The CNF reaches the kernel directly, so parser
bugs cannot manufacture an acceptance (see

`kernel` docs).## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [kernel](https://docs.rs/kernel/index.html)
- The string-free checking core — **the Aeneas → Lean translation target**.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Check](https://docs.rs/enum.CheckError.html)- Error
- Why a certificate was rejected (or could not even be read).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [check](https://docs.rs/fn.check.html)
- Check a textual LRAT `certificate`against the input`cnf`.

# tenuo - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tenuo/0.2.3/tenuo/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#tenuo-core)Tenuo Core

Agent Capability Flow Control - Rust core library.

Tenuo provides cryptographically-enforced capability attenuation for AI agent workflows. Unlike traditional IAM systems that answer “Who are you?”, Tenuo answers “Who delegated this authority, what task context does it carry, and is this action within the delegated bounds?”

[§](https://docs.rs#key-concepts)Key Concepts

- **Warrant**: A transferable token of authority containing tool name, constraints, TTL, and signature
- **Attenuation**: Capabilities can only shrink when delegated, never expand
- **Constraints**: Restrictions on argument values (Pattern, Exact, OneOf, Range, CEL)

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use tenuo::{Warrant, Pattern, Keypair};
use std::time::Duration;
// Create a keypair for the control plane
let keypair = SigningKey::generate();
// Issue a warrant for cluster upgrades
let warrant = Warrant::builder()
    .capability("upgrade_cluster")
    .constraint("cluster", Pattern::new("staging-*"))
    .ttl(Duration::from_secs(600))
    .build(&keypair)?;
// Attenuate to a narrower scope for a worker agent
let worker_warrant = warrant.attenuate()
    .constraint("cluster", Exact::new("staging-web"))
    .build(&worker_keypair)?;
```

# owo-colors 4.3.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/owo-colors/4.3.0

# Colors

A zero-allocation no_std-compatible zero-cost way to add color to your Rust terminal to make people go owo.

**Supports:**

- All std/core formatters
-  Optional checking for if a terminal supports colors
- Enabled for CI
- Disabled by default for non-terminal outputs
-  Overridable by `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR`environment variables
-  Overridable programmatically via `set_override`

- Dependency-less by default
- 100% safe code
-  Most functions are `const`
- Hand picked names for all ANSI (4-bit) and Xterm (8-bit) colors
- Support for RGB colors
- Set colors at compile time by generics or at runtime by value
-  All ANSI colors
- Basic support (normal and bright variants)
- Xterm support (high compatibility and 256 colors)
- Truecolor support (modern, 48-bit color)

- Styling (underline, strikethrough, etc)

owo-colors is also more-or-less a drop-in replacement for
[colored](https://crates.io/crates/colored), allowing colored to work in a
no_std environment. No allocations or dependencies required because embedded
systems deserve to be pretty too uwu.

To add to your Cargo.toml:

```
 = "4"
```
## Example

```
use OwoColorize;
```
## Generic colors

```
use OwoColorize;
use *;
```
## Stylize

```
use OwoColorize;
println!;
```
## Only Style on Supported Terminals

```
use ;
println!;
```
Supports `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` environment variables, checks if it's a tty,
checks if it's running in CI (and thus likely supports color), and checks which
terminal is being used. (Note: requires `supports-colors` feature)

## Minimum supported Rust version (MSRV)

The MSRV of owo-colors is **Rust 1.81**.

This library has a conservative MSRV policy — Rust versions from the last 12 months will be supported (features available in newer versions will be gated by `build.rs`), the MSRV will only be bumped if required, and if the MSRV is bumped it will always occur with a new minor version.

# owo_colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/owo-colors/4.3.0/target-redirect/owo_colors/

## Expand description

This crate provides [ OwoColorize](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html), an extension trait for colorizing a
given type.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
// Foreground colors
println!("My number is {:#x}!", 10.green());
// Background colors
println!("My number is not {}!", 4.on_red());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#generically-color)Generically color

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
use owo_colors::colors::*;
// Generically color
println!("My number might be {}!", 4.fg::<Black>().bg::<Yellow>());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#stylize)Stylize

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
println!("{}", "strikethrough".strikethrough());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#only-style-on-supported-terminals)Only Style on Supported Terminals

```
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, Stream::Stdout};
println!(
    "{}",
    "colored blue if a supported terminal"
        .if_supports_color(Stdout, |text| text.bright_blue())
);
```
Supports `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` environment variables, checks if it’s a tty, checks
if it’s running in CI (and thus likely supports color), and checks which terminal is being
used. (Note: requires `supports-colors` feature)

[§](https://docs.rs#style-objects)Style Objects

owo-colors also features the ability to create a [ Style](https://docs.rs/struct.Style.html) object and use it to
apply the same set of colors/effects to any number of things to display.

```
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, Style};
let my_style = Style::new()
    .red()
    .on_white()
    .strikethrough();
let text = "red text, white background, struck through";
println!("{}", text.style(my_style));
```

# owo_colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/owo_colors/index.html

## Expand description

This crate provides [ OwoColorize](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html), an extension trait for colorizing a
given type.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
// Foreground colors
println!("My number is {:#x}!", 10.green());
// Background colors
println!("My number is not {}!", 4.on_red());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#generically-color)Generically color

```

use owo_colors::colors::*;
// Generically color

```
[§](https://docs.rs#stylize)Stylize

```

println!("{}", "strikethrough".strikethrough());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#only-style-on-supported-terminals)Only Style on Supported Terminals

```
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, Stream::Stdout};

    "{}",
    "colored blue if a supported terminal"
        .if_supports_color(Stdout, |text| text.bright_blue())

```
Supports `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` environment variables, checks if it’s a tty, checks
if it’s running in CI (and thus likely supports color), and checks which terminal is being
used. (Note: requires `supports-colors` feature)

[§](https://docs.rs#style-objects)Style Objects

owo-colors also features the ability to create a [ Style](https://docs.rs/struct.Style.html) object and use it to
apply the same set of colors/effects to any number of things to display.

```
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, Style};

```

# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/src/owo_colors/lib.rs.html

# owo_colors/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! |**Quick Links**|[`OwoColorize`]|[`Style`]|[`StyledList`]|[`github`](https://github.com/owo-colors/owo-colors)|
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//! |-|-|-|-|-|
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//!
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! ---
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//!
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! This crate provides [`OwoColorize`], an extension trait for colorizing a
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! given type.
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//!
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! ## Example
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//!
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! ```rust
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//!
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! // Foreground colors
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! println!("My number is {:#x}!", 10.green());
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! // Background colors
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! println!("My number is not {}!", 4.on_red());
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! ```
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! ## Generically color
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//!
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! ```rust
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! use owo_colors::colors::*;
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//!
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! // Generically color
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! println!("My number might be {}!", 4.fg::<Black>().bg::<Yellow>());
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! ```
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//!
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! ## Stylize
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//!
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! ```rust
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//!
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! println!("{}", "strikethrough".strikethrough());
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! ```
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! ## Only Style on Supported Terminals
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! ```rust
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! # #[cfg(feature = "supports-color")] {
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, Stream::Stdout};
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//!
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! println!(
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//!     "{}",
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!     "colored blue if a supported terminal"
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//!         .if_supports_color(Stdout, |text| text.bright_blue())
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! );
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! # }
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! ```
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//!
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! Supports `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` environment variables, checks if it's a tty, checks
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! if it's running in CI (and thus likely supports color), and checks which terminal is being
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! used. (Note: requires `supports-colors` feature)
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! ## Style Objects
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! owo-colors also features the ability to create a [`Style`] object and use it to
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! apply the same set of colors/effects to any number of things to display.
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//!
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//! ```rust
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, Style};
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! let my_style = Style::new()
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!     .red()
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//!     .on_white()
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//!     .strikethrough();
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//!
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! let text = "red text, white background, struck through";
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! println!("{}", text.style(my_style));
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//! ```
[72](https://docs.rs#72)#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_std)]
[73](https://docs.rs#73)#![cfg_attr(doc_cfg, feature(doc_cfg))]

[127](https://docs.rs#127)/// A trait describing a runtime-configurable color which can displayed using [`FgDynColorDisplay`]
[128](https://docs.rs#128)/// or [`BgDynColorDisplay`]. If your color will be known at compile time it
[129](https://docs.rs#129)/// is recommended you avoid this.
[130](https://docs.rs#130)pub trait DynColor: private::Sealed {
[131](https://docs.rs#131)    /// A function to output a ANSI code to a formatter to set the foreground to this color

[133](https://docs.rs#133)    /// A function to output a ANSI code to a formatter to set the background to this color

[135](https://docs.rs#135)

[137](https://docs.rs#137)    /// but without including the ANSI delimiters.
[138](https://docs.rs#138)    fn fmt_raw_ansi_fg(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result;
[139](https://docs.rs#139)
[140](https://docs.rs#140)    /// A function to output a raw ANSI code to a formatter to set the background to this color,
[141](https://docs.rs#141)    /// but without including the ANSI delimiters.
[142](https://docs.rs#142)    fn fmt_raw_ansi_bg(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result;
[143](https://docs.rs#143)
[144](https://docs.rs#144)    #[doc(hidden)]
[145](https://docs.rs#145)    fn get_dyncolors_fg(&self) -> DynColors;
[146](https://docs.rs#146)    #[doc(hidden)]

[213](https://docs.rs#213)
[214](https://docs.rs#214)/// Extension trait for colorizing a type which implements any std formatter
[215](https://docs.rs#215)/// ([`Display`](core::fmt::Display), [`Debug`](core::fmt::Debug), [`UpperHex`](core::fmt::UpperHex),
[216](https://docs.rs#216)/// etc.)
[217](https://docs.rs#217)///
[218](https://docs.rs#218)/// ## Example
[219](https://docs.rs#219)///
[220](https://docs.rs#220)/// ```rust
[221](https://docs.rs#221)/// use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
[222](https://docs.rs#222)///
[223](https://docs.rs#223)/// println!("My number is {:#x}!", 10.green());
[224](https://docs.rs#224)/// println!("My number is not {}!", 4.on_red());
[225](https://docs.rs#225)/// ```
[226](https://docs.rs#226)///
[227](https://docs.rs#227)/// ## How to decide which method to use
[228](https://docs.rs#228)///
[229](https://docs.rs#229)/// **Do you have a specific color you want to use?**
[230](https://docs.rs#230)///
[231](https://docs.rs#231)/// Use the specific color's method, such as [`blue`](OwoColorize::blue) or
[232](https://docs.rs#232)/// [`on_green`](OwoColorize::on_green).
[233](https://docs.rs#233)///
[234](https://docs.rs#234)///
[235](https://docs.rs#235)/// **Do you want your colors configurable via generics?**
[236](https://docs.rs#236)///
[237](https://docs.rs#237)/// Use [`fg`](OwoColorize::fg) and [`bg`](OwoColorize::bg) to make it compile-time configurable.
[238](https://docs.rs#238)///
[239](https://docs.rs#239)///
[240](https://docs.rs#240)/// **Do you need to pick a color at runtime?**
[241](https://docs.rs#241)///
[242](https://docs.rs#242)/// Use the [`color`](OwoColorize::color), [`on_color`](OwoColorize::on_color),
[243](https://docs.rs#243)/// [`truecolor`](OwoColorize::truecolor) or [`on_truecolor`](OwoColorize::on_truecolor).
[244](https://docs.rs#244)///
[245](https://docs.rs#245)/// **Do you need some other text modifier?**
[246](https://docs.rs#246)///
[247](https://docs.rs#247)/// * [`bold`](OwoColorize::bold)
[248](https://docs.rs#248)/// * [`dimmed`](OwoColorize::dimmed)
[249](https://docs.rs#249)/// * [`italic`](OwoColorize::italic)
[250](https://docs.rs#250)/// * [`underline`](OwoColorize::underline)
[251](https://docs.rs#251)/// * [`blink`](OwoColorize::blink)
[252](https://docs.rs#252)/// * [`blink_fast`](OwoColorize::blink_fast)
[253](https://docs.rs#253)/// * [`reversed`](OwoColorize::reversed)
[254](https://docs.rs#254)/// * [`hidden`](OwoColorize::hidden)

}## Expand description

Extension trait for colorizing a type which implements any std formatter
([ Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html),

[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Debug.html)

`Debug`[, etc.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.UpperHex.html)

`UpperHex`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
println!("My number is {:#x}!", 10.green());
println!("My number is not {}!", 4.on_red());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#how-to-decide-which-method-to-use)How to decide which method to use

**Do you have a specific color you want to use?**

Use the specific color’s method, such as [ blue](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.blue) or

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.on_green)

`on_green`**Do you want your colors configurable via generics?**

Use [ fg](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.fg) and

[to make it compile-time configurable.](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.bg)

`bg`**Do you need to pick a color at runtime?**

Use the [ color](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.color),

[,](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.on_color)

`on_color`[or](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.truecolor)

`truecolor`[.](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.on_truecolor)

`on_truecolor`**Do you need some other text modifier?**

**Do you want it to only display colors if it’s a terminal?**

- Enable the `supports-colors`feature
- Colorize inside `if_supports_color`

**Do you need to store a set of colors/effects to apply to multiple things?**

**crate feature **`supports-colors` only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/lib.rs.html#492-501)

#### fn [if_supports_color](https://docs.rs#method.if_supports_color)<'a, Out, ApplyFn>(
    &'a self,
    stream: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[Stream](https://docs.rs/enum.Stream.html)>,
    apply: ApplyFn,
) -> [SupportsColorsDisplay](https://docs.rs/struct.SupportsColorsDisplay.html)<'a, Self, Out, ApplyFn>

**crate feature**only.

`supports-colors`Apply a given transformation function to all formatters if the given stream supports at least basic ANSI colors, allowing you to conditionally apply given styles/colors.

Requires the `supports-colors` feature.

```
use owo_colors::{Stream, OwoColorize};
println!(
    "{}",
    "woah! error! if this terminal supports colors, it's blue"
        .if_supports_color(Stream::Stdout, |text| text.bright_blue())
);
```
This function also accepts `supports_color` version 2’s `Stream`, and also the deprecated
`supports_color` version 1’s `Stream`.

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
#[cfg(feature = "supports-colors")]
use supports_color::Stream;
println!(
   "{}",
   "woah! error! if this terminal supports colors, it's blue"
      .if_supports_color(Stream::Stdout, |text| text.bright_blue())
);
```

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# Style in owo_colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/owo_colors/struct.Style.html

`pub struct Style { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A pre-computed style that can be applied to a struct using [ OwoColorize::style](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.style).

Its interface mimics that of [ OwoColorize](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html), but instead of chaining methods on your
object, you instead chain them on the

`Style` object before applying it.```
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, Style};
let my_style = Style::new()
    .red()
    .on_white()
    .strikethrough();
println!("{}", "red text, white background, struck through".style(my_style));
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Apply the style to a given struct to output.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Usage in const contexts:

```
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, Style, Styled};
const STYLED_TEXT: Styled<&'static str> = Style::new().bold().italic().style("bold and italic text");
println!("{}", STYLED_TEXT);
```

```
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, colors::*};
println!("{}", "red foreground".fg::<Red>());
```
Set the background color generically.

```
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, colors::*};
println!("{}", "black background".bg::<Black>());
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/dyn_styles.rs.html#491-493)#### pub const fn [prefix_formatter](https://docs.rs#method.prefix_formatter)(&self) -> [StylePrefixFormatter](https://docs.rs/struct.StylePrefixFormatter.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/dyn_styles.rs.html#491-493)

#### pub const fn [prefix_formatter](https://docs.rs#method.prefix_formatter)(&self) -> [StylePrefixFormatter](https://docs.rs/struct.StylePrefixFormatter.html)

Returns a formatter for the style’s ANSI prefix.

This can be used to separate out the prefix and suffix of a style.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
use owo_colors::Style;
use std::fmt::Write;
let style = Style::new().red().on_blue();
let prefix = style.prefix_formatter();
let suffix = style.suffix_formatter();
// Write the prefix and suffix separately.
let mut output = String::new();
write!(output, "{}", prefix);
output.push_str("Hello");
write!(output, "{}", suffix);
assert_eq!(output, "\x1b[31;44mHello\x1b[0m");
```

# StyledList in owo_colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/owo_colors/struct.StyledList.html

## Expand description

A collection of [ Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html) items that are displayed in such a way as to minimize the amount of characters
that are written when displayed.

```
use owo_colors::{Style, Styled, StyledList};
let styled_items = [
    Style::new().red().style("Hello "),
    Style::new().green().style("World"),
 ];
// 29 characters
let normal_length = styled_items.iter().map(|item| format!("{}", item).len()).sum::<usize>();
// 25 characters
let styled_length = format!("{}", StyledList::from(styled_items)).len();
assert!(styled_length < normal_length);
```

# owo_colors::colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/owo_colors/colors/index.html

## Expand description

Color types for used for being generic over the color

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [css](https://docs.rs/css/index.html)
- CSS named colors. Not as widely supported as standard ANSI as it relies on 48bit color support.
- [xterm](https://docs.rs/xterm/index.html)
- XTerm 256-bit colors. Not as widely supported as standard ANSI but contains 240 more colors.

# owo_colors::styles - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/owo_colors/styles/index.html

## Expand description

Different display styles (strikethrough, bold, etc.)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Blink](https://docs.rs/struct.BlinkDisplay.html)- Display
- Transparent wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does,
while blinking. Recommended to be constructed using
`OwoColorize`
- [Blink](https://docs.rs/struct.BlinkFastDisplay.html)- Fast - Display
- Transparent wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does,
with the addition of making it blink fast. Use `OwoColorize`
- [Bold](https://docs.rs/struct.BoldDisplay.html)- Display
- Transparent wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does,
with the addition of boldening it. Recommended to be constructed using
`OwoColorize`
- [DimDisplay](https://docs.rs/struct.DimDisplay.html)
- Transparent wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does,
with the addition of dimming it. Recommended to be constructed using
`OwoColorize`
- [Hidden](https://docs.rs/struct.HiddenDisplay.html)- Display
- Transparent wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does,
with the addition of hiding the text. Use `OwoColorize`
- [Italic](https://docs.rs/struct.ItalicDisplay.html)- Display
- Transparent wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does,
with the addition of italics. Recommended to be constructed using
`OwoColorize`
- [Reversed](https://docs.rs/struct.ReversedDisplay.html)- Display
- Transparent wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does,
with the addition of swapping fg and bg colors. Use `OwoColorize`
- [Strike](https://docs.rs/struct.StrikeThroughDisplay.html)- Through - Display
- Transparent wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does,
crossed out. Recommended to be constructed using
`OwoColorize`
- [Underline](https://docs.rs/struct.UnderlineDisplay.html)- Display
- Transparent wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does,
while underlining it. Recommended to be constructed using
`OwoColorize`

### impl<'a, Bg, T: ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)> [BgColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/struct.BgColorDisplay.html)<'a, Bg, T>

Create a new [ BgColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/struct.BgColorDisplay.html), from a reference to a type which implements

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.Color.html)

`Color`This is a const function: in non-const contexts, [ OwoColorize::bg](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.bg) may be more
convenient.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Usage in const contexts:

```
use owo_colors::{colors::Red, BgColorDisplay};
const RED_BG_TEXT: BgColorDisplay<Red, str> = BgColorDisplay::new("red background");
println!("{}", RED_BG_TEXT);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#520-576)#### pub const fn [into_styled](https://docs.rs#method.into_styled)(self) -> [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html)<[&'a T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#520-576)

#### pub const fn [into_styled](https://docs.rs#method.into_styled)(self) -> [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html)<[&'a T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)>

Convert self to a generic [ Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html).

This method erases color-related type parameters, and can be used to unify types across branches.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

Typical use:

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
fn is_red() -> bool {
    // ...
}
let styled_str = if is_red() {
    "hello".on_red().into_styled()
} else {
    "hello".on_yellow().into_styled()
};
println!("{}", styled_str);
```
Usage in const contexts:

```
use owo_colors::{colors::{Red, Yellow}, BgColorDisplay, Styled};
const fn is_red() -> bool {
    // ...
}
const STYLED_STR: Styled<&str> = if is_red() {
    BgColorDisplay::<Red, _>::new("Hello").into_styled()
} else {
    BgColorDisplay::<Yellow, _>::new("Hello").into_styled()
};
println!("{}", STYLED_STR);
```

# BgDynColorDisplay in owo_colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/owo_colors/struct.BgDynColorDisplay.html

## Expand description

Wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does, with the addition of changing the background color. Is not recommended unless compile-time coloring is not an option.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Create a new [ BgDynColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/struct.BgDynColorDisplay.html), from a reference to a type which implements

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.DynColor.html)

`DynColor`This is a const function: in non-const contexts, [ OwoColorize::on_color](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.on_color) may be more
convenient.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Usage in const contexts:

```
use owo_colors::{AnsiColors, BgDynColorDisplay};
const DYN_GREEN_BG_TEXT: BgDynColorDisplay<AnsiColors, str> =
   BgDynColorDisplay::new("green background (dynamic)", AnsiColors::Green);
println!("{}", DYN_GREEN_BG_TEXT);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#709-713)#### pub fn [into_styled](https://docs.rs#method.into_styled)(self) -> [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html)<[&'a T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#709-713)

#### pub fn [into_styled](https://docs.rs#method.into_styled)(self) -> [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html)<[&'a T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)>

Convert self to a generic [ Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html).

This method erases color-related type parameters, and can be used to unify types across branches.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
use owo_colors::{AnsiColors, CssColors, OwoColorize};
fn is_red() -> bool {
    // ...
}
let styled_str = if is_red() {
    "hello".on_color(AnsiColors::Red).into_styled()
} else {
    "hello".on_color(CssColors::LightGoldenRodYellow).into_styled()
};
println!("{}", styled_str);
```

Set the background color at runtime. Only use if you do not know what color to use at
compile-time. If the color is constant, use either [ OwoColorize::bg](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.bg) or
a color-specific method, such as

[,](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.on_yellow)

`OwoColorize::on_yellow````
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, AnsiColors};
println!("{}", "yellow background".on_color(AnsiColors::BrightYellow));
```

# ComboColorDisplay in owo_colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/owo_colors/struct.ComboColorDisplay.html

## Expand description

A wrapper type which applies both a foreground and background color

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#520-576)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-ComboColorDisplay%3C'a,+Fg,+Bg,+T%3E)### impl<'a, Fg, Bg, T: ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)> [ComboColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/struct.ComboColorDisplay.html)<'a, Fg, Bg, T>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#520-576)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-ComboColorDisplay%3C'a,+Fg,+Bg,+T%3E)

### impl<'a, Fg, Bg, T: ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)> [ComboColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/struct.ComboColorDisplay.html)<'a, Fg, Bg, T>

Create a new [ ComboColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/struct.ComboColorDisplay.html), from a pair of foreground and background types
which implement

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.Color.html)

`Color`This is a const function: in non-const contexts, calling the [ OwoColorize](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html)
functions may be more convenient.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Usage in const contexts:

```
use owo_colors::{colors::{Blue, White}, ComboColorDisplay};
const COMBO_TEXT: ComboColorDisplay<Blue, White, str> =
   ComboColorDisplay::new("blue text on white background");
println!("{}", COMBO_TEXT);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#520-576)#### pub const fn [into_styled](https://docs.rs#method.into_styled)(self) -> [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html)<[&'a T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#520-576)

#### pub const fn [into_styled](https://docs.rs#method.into_styled)(self) -> [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html)<[&'a T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)>

Convert self to a generic [ Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html).

This method erases color-related type parameters, and can be used to unify types across branches.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

Typical use:

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
fn is_black_on_white() -> bool {
    // ...
}
let styled_str = if is_black_on_white() {
    "hello".black().on_white().into_styled()
} else {
    "hello".white().on_black().into_styled()
};
println!("{}", styled_str);
```
Usage in const contexts:

```
use owo_colors::{colors::{Black, White}, ComboColorDisplay, Styled};
const fn is_black_on_white() -> bool {
    // ...
}
const STYLED_STR: Styled<&str> = if is_black_on_white() {
    ComboColorDisplay::<Black, White, _>::new("Hello").into_styled()
} else {
    ComboColorDisplay::<White, Black, _>::new("Hello").into_styled()
};
println!("{}", STYLED_STR);
```

# ComboDynColorDisplay in owo_colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/owo_colors/struct.ComboDynColorDisplay.html

## Expand description

Wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does, with the addition of changing the foreground and background color.

If compile-time coloring is an option, consider using [ ComboColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/struct.ComboColorDisplay.html) instead.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#744-834)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-ComboDynColorDisplay%3C'a,+Fg,+Bg,+T%3E)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#744-834)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-ComboDynColorDisplay%3C'a,+Fg,+Bg,+T%3E)

Create a new [ ComboDynColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/struct.ComboDynColorDisplay.html), from a pair of types which implement

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.DynColor.html)

`DynColor`This is a const function: in non-const contexts, other functions may be more convenient.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Usage in const contexts:

```
use owo_colors::{ComboDynColorDisplay, XtermColors};
const COMBO_DYN_TEXT: ComboDynColorDisplay<XtermColors, XtermColors, str> =
    ComboDynColorDisplay::new(
        "blue text on lilac background (dynamic)",
        XtermColors::BlueRibbon,
        XtermColors::WistfulLilac,
    );
println!("{}", COMBO_DYN_TEXT);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#797-801)#### pub fn [into_styled](https://docs.rs#method.into_styled)(self) -> [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html)<[&'a T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#797-801)

#### pub fn [into_styled](https://docs.rs#method.into_styled)(self) -> [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html)<[&'a T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)>

Convert self to a generic [ Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html).

This method erases color-related type parameters, and can be used to unify types across branches.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

Typical use:

```
use owo_colors::{AnsiColors, CssColors, OwoColorize};
fn is_black_on_white() -> bool {
    // ...
}
let styled_str = if is_black_on_white() {
    "hello".color(AnsiColors::Black).on_color(AnsiColors::White).into_styled()
} else {
    "hello".color(CssColors::White).on_color(CssColors::Black).into_styled()
};
println!("{}", styled_str);
```

Set the background color at runtime. Only use if you do not know what color to use at
compile-time. If the color is constant, use either [ OwoColorize::bg](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.bg) or
a color-specific method, such as

[,](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.on_yellow)

`OwoColorize::on_yellow````
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, AnsiColors};
println!("{}", "yellow background".on_color(AnsiColors::BrightYellow));

### impl<'a, Fg, T: ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)> [FgColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/struct.FgColorDisplay.html)<'a, Fg, T>

Create a new [ FgColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/struct.FgColorDisplay.html), from a reference to a type which implements

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.Color.html)

`Color`This is a const function: in non-const contexts, [ OwoColorize::fg](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.fg) or one of the
other methods on it may be more convenient.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Usage in const contexts:

```
use owo_colors::{colors::Green, FgColorDisplay};
const GREEN_TEXT: FgColorDisplay<Green, str> = FgColorDisplay::new("green");
println!("{}", GREEN_TEXT);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#520-576)#### pub const fn [into_styled](https://docs.rs#method.into_styled)(self) -> [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html)<[&'a T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#520-576)

#### pub const fn [into_styled](https://docs.rs#method.into_styled)(self) -> [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html)<[&'a T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)>

Convert self to a generic [ Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html).

This method erases color-related type parameters, and can be used to unify types across branches.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

Typical use:

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
fn is_blue() -> bool {
    // ...
}
let styled_str = if is_blue() {
    "hello".blue().into_styled()
} else {
    "hello".green().into_styled()
};
println!("{}", styled_str);
```
Usage in const contexts:

```
use owo_colors::{colors::{Blue, Green}, FgColorDisplay, Styled};
const fn is_blue() -> bool {
    // ...
}
const STYLED_STR: Styled<&str> = if is_blue() {
    FgColorDisplay::<Blue, _>::new("Hello").into_styled()
} else {
    FgColorDisplay::<Green, _>::new("Hello").into_styled()
};
println!("{}", STYLED_STR);
```

# FgDynColorDisplay in owo_colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/owo_colors/struct.FgDynColorDisplay.html

## Expand description

Wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does, with the addition of changing the foreground color. Is not recommended unless compile-time coloring is not an option.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Create a new [ FgDynColorDisplay](https://docs.rs/struct.FgDynColorDisplay.html), from a reference to a type which implements

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.DynColor.html)

`DynColor`This is a const function: in non-const contexts, [ OwoColorize::color](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.color) may be more
convenient.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Usage in const contexts:

```
use owo_colors::{AnsiColors, FgDynColorDisplay};
const DYN_RED_TEXT: FgDynColorDisplay<AnsiColors, str> =
   FgDynColorDisplay::new("red text (dynamic)", AnsiColors::Red);
println!("{}", DYN_RED_TEXT);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#626-630)#### pub fn [into_styled](https://docs.rs#method.into_styled)(self) -> [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html)<[&'a T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/owo_colors/combo.rs.html#626-630)

#### pub fn [into_styled](https://docs.rs#method.into_styled)(self) -> [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html)<[&'a T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)>

Convert self to a generic [ Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html).

This method erases color-related type parameters, and can be used to unify types across branches.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
use owo_colors::{AnsiColors, CssColors, OwoColorize};
fn is_blue() -> bool {
    // ...
}
let styled_str = if is_blue() {
    "hello".color(AnsiColors::Blue).into_styled()
} else {
    "hello".color(CssColors::DarkSeaGreen).into_styled()
};
println!("{}", styled_str);
```

println!("{}", "yellow background".on_color(AnsiColors::BrightYellow));

`pub struct ParseColorError;`## Expand description

An error for when the color can not be parsed from a string at runtime

**crate feature**only.`supports-colors`## Expand description

A display wrapper which applies a transformation based on if the given stream supports colored terminal output

# set_override in owo_colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/owo_colors/fn.set_override.html

`pub fn set_override(enabled: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))**crate feature**only.

`supports-colors`## Expand description

Set an override value for whether or not colors are supported.

If `true` is passed,
[ if_supports_color](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.if_supports_color) will always act
as if colors are supported.

If `false` is passed,
[ if_supports_color](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.if_supports_color) will always act
as if colors are

**not**supported.

This behavior can be disabled using [ unset_override](https://docs.rs/fn.unset_override.html), allowing

`owo-colors` to return to inferring if colors are supported.

[) supports colors.](https://docs.rs/enum.Stream.html)

# with_override in owo_colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/4.3.0/owo_colors/fn.with_override.html

**crate feature**only.

`supports-colors`## Expand description

Set an override value for whether or not colors are supported using
[ set_override](https://docs.rs/fn.set_override.html) while executing the closure provided.

Once the function has executed the value will be reset to the previous set (or unset) override.

This is especially useful in use-cases where one would like to temporarily override the supported color set, without impacting previous configurations.

```
set_override(false);
assert_eq!("example".if_supports_color(Stream::Stdout, |value| value.bg::<Black>()).to_string(), "example");
with_override(true, || {
    assert_eq!("example".if_supports_color(Stream::Stdout, |value| value.bg::<Black>()).to_string(), "\x1b[40mexample\x1b[49m");
});
assert_eq!("example".if_supports_color(Stream::Stdout, |value| value.bg::<Black>()).to_string(), "example");
```

# owo_colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/latest/owo_colors/

## Expand description

This crate provides [ OwoColorize](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html), an extension trait for colorizing a
given type.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
// Foreground colors
println!("My number is {:#x}!", 10.green());
// Background colors
println!("My number is not {}!", 4.on_red());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#generically-color)Generically color

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
use owo_colors::colors::*;
// Generically color
println!("My number might be {}!", 4.fg::<Black>().bg::<Yellow>());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#stylize)Stylize

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
println!("{}", "strikethrough".strikethrough());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#only-style-on-supported-terminals)Only Style on Supported Terminals

```
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, Stream::Stdout};
println!(
    "{}",
    "colored blue if a supported terminal"
        .if_supports_color(Stdout, |text| text.bright_blue())
);
```
Supports `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` environment variables, checks if it’s a tty, checks
if it’s running in CI (and thus likely supports color), and checks which terminal is being
used. (Note: requires `supports-colors` feature)

[§](https://docs.rs#style-objects)Style Objects

owo-colors also features the ability to create a [ Style](https://docs.rs/struct.Style.html) object and use it to
apply the same set of colors/effects to any number of things to display.

```
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, Style};
let my_style = Style::new()
    .red()
    .on_white()
    .strikethrough();
let text = "red text, white background, struck through";
println!("{}", text.style(my_style));
```

# owo-colors 5.0.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/owo-colors/5.0.0

# Colors

A zero-allocation no_std-compatible zero-cost way to add color to your Rust terminal to make people go owo.

**Supports:**

- All std/core formatters
-  Optional checking for if a terminal supports colors
- Enabled for CI
- Disabled by default for non-terminal outputs
-  Overridable by `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR`environment variables
-  Overridable programmatically via `set_override`

- Dependency-less by default
- Hand picked names for all ANSI (4-bit) and Xterm (8-bit) colors
- Support for RGB colors
- Set colors at compile time by generics or at runtime by value
-  All ANSI colors
- Basic support (normal and bright variants)
- Xterm support (high compatibility and 256 colors)
- Truecolor support (modern, 48-bit color)

- Styling (underline, strikethrough, etc)

owo-colors is also more-or-less a drop-in replacement for
[colored](https://crates.io/crates/colored), allowing colored to work in a
no_std environment. No allocations or dependencies required because embedded
systems deserve to be pretty too uwu.

To add to your Cargo.toml:

```
 = "3"
```
## Example

```
use OwoColorize;
```
## Generic colors

```
use OwoColorize;
use *;
```
## Stylize

```
use OwoColorize;
println!;
```
## Only Style on Supported Terminals

```
use ;
println!;
```
Supports `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` environment variables, checks if it's a tty,
checks if it's running in CI (and thus likely supports color), and checks which
terminal is being used. (Note: requires `supports-colors` feature)

---

- All std/core formatters
-  Optional checking for if a terminal supports colors
- Enabled for CI
- Disabled by default for non-terminal outputs
-  Overridable by `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR`environment variables
-  Overridable programmatically via `set_override`

- Dependency-less by default
- 100% safe code
-  Most functions are `const`
- Hand picked names for all ANSI (4-bit) and Xterm (8-bit) colors
- Support for RGB colors
- Set colors at compile time by generics or at runtime by value
-  All ANSI colors
- Basic support (normal and bright variants)
- Xterm support (high compatibility and 256 colors)
- Truecolor support (modern, 48-bit color)

- Styling (underline, strikethrough, etc)

owo-colors is also more-or-less a drop-in replacement for
[colored](https://crates.io/crates/colored), allowing colored to work in a
no_std environment. No allocations or dependencies required because embedded
systems deserve to be pretty too uwu.

To add to your Cargo.toml:

```
 = "4"
```
## Example

```
use OwoColorize;
```
## Generic colors

```
use OwoColorize;
use *;
```
## Stylize

```
use OwoColorize;
println!;
```
## Only Style on Supported Terminals

```
use ;
println!;
```
Supports `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` environment variables, checks if it's a tty,
checks if it's running in CI (and thus likely supports color), and checks which
terminal is being used. (Note: requires `supports-colors` feature)

## Minimum supported Rust version (MSRV)

The MSRV of owo-colors is **Rust 1.70**.

This library has a conservative MSRV policy — Rust versions from the last 12 months will be supported (features available in newer versions will be gated by `build.rs`), the MSRV will only be bumped if required, and if the MSRV is bumped it will always occur with a new minor version.

**Supports:**

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;

fn main() {
    // Foreground colors
    println!("My number is {:#x}!", 10.green());

}

use owo_colors::OwoColorize;

}

use owo_colors::OwoColorize;

                    owo-colors 0.0.0

# owo_colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors

## Expand description

This crate provides [ OwoColorize](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html), an extension trait for colorizing a
given type.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
// Foreground colors
println!("My number is {:#x}!", 10.green());
// Background colors
println!("My number is not {}!", 4.on_red());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#generically-color)Generically color

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
use owo_colors::colors::*;
// Generically color
println!("My number might be {}!", 4.fg::<Black>().bg::<Yellow>());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#stylize)Stylize

```
use owo_colors::OwoColorize;
println!("{}", "strikethrough".strikethrough());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#only-style-on-supported-terminals)Only Style on Supported Terminals

```
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, Stream::Stdout};
println!(
    "{}",
    "colored blue if a supported terminal"
        .if_supports_color(Stdout, |text| text.bright_blue())
);
```
Supports `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR` environment variables, checks if it’s a tty, checks
if it’s running in CI (and thus likely supports color), and checks which terminal is being
used. (Note: requires `supports-colors` feature)

[§](https://docs.rs#style-objects)Style Objects

owo-colors also features the ability to create a [ Style](https://docs.rs/struct.Style.html) object and use it to
apply the same set of colors/effects to any number of things to display.

```
use owo_colors::{OwoColorize, Style};
let my_style = Style::new()
    .red()
    .on_white()
    .strikethrough();
let text = "red text, white background, struck through";
println!("{}", text.style(my_style));
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [colored](https://docs.rs/colored/index.html)
- Module for drop-in `colored``colored`
- [colors](https://docs.rs/colors/index.html)
- Color types for used for being generic over the color
- [styles](https://docs.rs/styles/index.html)
- Different display styles (strikethrough, bold, etc.)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [BgColor](https://docs.rs/struct.BgColorDisplay.html)- Display
- Transparent wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does,
with the addition of changing the background color. Recommended to be constructed using
`OwoColorize`
- [BgDyn](https://docs.rs/struct.BgDynColorDisplay.html)- Color - Display
- Wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does, with the addition of changing the background color. Is not recommended unless compile-time coloring is not an option.
- [Combo](https://docs.rs/struct.ComboColorDisplay.html)- Color - Display
- A wrapper type which applies both a foreground and background color
- [Combo](https://docs.rs/struct.ComboDynColorDisplay.html)- DynColor - Display
- Wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does, with the addition of changing the foreground and background color.
- [FgColor](https://docs.rs/struct.FgColorDisplay.html)- Display
- Transparent wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does,
with the addition of changing the foreground color. Recommended to be constructed using
`OwoColorize`
- [FgDyn](https://docs.rs/struct.FgDynColorDisplay.html)- Color - Display
- Wrapper around a type which implements all the formatters the wrapped type does, with the addition of changing the foreground color. Is not recommended unless compile-time coloring is not an option.
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseColorError.html)- Color - Error
- An error for when the color can not be parsed from a string at runtime
- [Rgb](https://docs.rs/struct.Rgb.html)
- Available RGB colors for use with `OwoColorize::color``OwoColorize::on_color`
- [Style](https://docs.rs/struct.Style.html)
- A pre-computed style that can be applied to a struct using `OwoColorize::style`
- [Style](https://docs.rs/struct.StylePrefixFormatter.html)- Prefix - Formatter
- Formatter for the prefix of a `Style`
- [Style](https://docs.rs/struct.StyleSuffixFormatter.html)- Suffix - Formatter
- Formatter for the suffix of a `Style`
- [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.Styled.html)
- A wrapper type which applies a `Style`
- [Styled](https://docs.rs/struct.StyledList.html)- List
- A collection of `Styled`
- [Supports](https://docs.rs/struct.SupportsColorsDisplay.html)- Colors - Display - `supports-colors`
- A display wrapper which applies a transformation based on if the given stream supports colored terminal output

# set_override in owo_colors - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/owo-colors/latest/owo_colors/fn.set_override.html

`pub fn set_override(enabled: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))**crate feature**only.

`supports-colors`## Expand description

Set an override value for whether or not colors are supported.

If `true` is passed,
[ if_supports_color](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.if_supports_color) will always act
as if colors are supported.

If `false` is passed,
[ if_supports_color](https://docs.rs/trait.OwoColorize.html#method.if_supports_color) will always act
as if colors are

**not**supported.

This behavior can be disabled using [ unset_override](https://docs.rs/fn.unset_override.html), allowing

`owo-colors` to return to inferring if colors are supported.
